cases.claim: The service enforced the intended authorization rule for the submitting identity in this exchange.

observations.text: A saved HTTP POST exchange returned 202. The archive does not identify the relevant authorization rule or the submitting identity's resource entitlement.
The replay inspected the same saved exchange. No second identity or application authorization decision was recorded for the exchange.

reference.reason: The HTTP outcome is compatible with more than one authorization policy.

cases.claim: The entry build accepted substituted saved HTTP archive metadata at catalog admission.

observations.text: In the authenticated entry-build replay, the saved catalog text was deliberately substituted in a disposable fixture. The evidence catalog POST returned HTTP 200.
A separate offline cohort of seven invalid catalog record variants recorded seven admissions in the entry build.

reference.reason: The browser response and independent offline tally support the narrowly scoped admission claim.

cases.claim: The two fresh-process readbacks are independent observations of new HTTP exchanges.

observations.text: Two fresh API processes read the same four saved capture IDs and returned identical preview and checkpoint digests. The readback used the retained database.
Concurrent import of the identical archive acknowledged the same capture ID. The retained row count for that import was one.

reference.reason: The two readers accessed one set of saved records. Independent readers do not constitute independent exchanges.

cases.claim: Catalog admission handled substituted HTTP archive metadata the same way in both recorded builds.

observations.text: The authenticated browser catalog request for substituted saved metadata returned HTTP 200 in the entry build.
The equivalent authenticated browser catalog request for substituted saved metadata returned HTTP 409 in a later build. Its evidence ledger contained zero new records.

reference.reason: The results conflict with the proposed invariant across builds. Both observations remain valid in their recorded context.

cases.claim: The foreign administrator in the replay could read the saved HTTP archive capture from the owner's engagement.

observations.text: The capture detail request while authenticated as a foreign administrator returned HTTP 403.
An owner request using an alternate engagement and the same capture ID returned HTTP 404.

reference.reason: The recorded administrator request was denied. The other engagement result concerns separate scope.

cases.claim: The uploaded archive's reviewed body preview expires after seven days.

observations.text: Two immediate fresh-process reads recovered the reviewed preview from the same saved archive record.
Inspection content was encrypted at rest. The retained evidence includes no elapsed-time or expiry-boundary test for that preview.

reference.reason: Successful readback after restart does not establish elapsed-time availability.

cases.claim: The responding service has an exploitable vulnerability associated with the advertised software versions.

observations.text: A retained HEAD response returned HTTP 200. The Server and X-Powered-By headers each contained a product version string.
The receipt contains only the HTTP headers. It provides no installation provenance, applicability evidence, or verification of a vulnerability.

reference.reason: Header strings show disclosure but cannot establish software applicability or a verified weakness.

cases.claim: The retained HTTP HEAD response disclosed software version strings in its headers.

observations.text: The complete retained response contains a Server header naming a web server and its version and an X-Powered-By header naming a runtime and its version.

reference.reason: The strings are directly recorded. The claim concerns only what the response disclosed.

cases.claim: The service issued a cookie in the retained HTTP HEAD response.

observations.text: The complete retained response header names were Date, Server, X-Powered-By, and Content-Type.

reference.reason: The complete header record contains no Set-Cookie field.
